definitions.definition: Ampere’s circuital law, given by Andre Marie Peter Ampere in 1826, relates the integrated magnetic field in a loop around a current-carrying wire to the current passing through the wire. Ampère’s circuital law states that, for any closed loop, the sum of each length element multiplied by the component of magnetic field parallel to that element is proportional to the current enclosed by the path. Σ B⃗ · Δl⃗ = μ₀ I
definitions.definitionUrdu: 1826 میں آندرے میری پیٹر ایمپیئر کا پیش کردہ دوری قانون، کرنٹ بردار تار کے گرد حلقے میں مقناطیسی میدان کے تکمل کو تار سے گزرنے والی برقی رو سے مربوط کرتا ہے۔ ایمپیئر کا دوری قانون کہتا ہے کہ کسی بھی بند حلقے میں ہر طولی عنصر اور اس عنصر کے متوازی مقناطیسی میدان کے جزو کے حاصلِ ضرب کا مجموعہ، اس راستے کے اندر محصور برقی رو کے متناسب ہوتا ہے۔ Σ B⃗ · Δl⃗ = μ₀ I
definitions.definitionPashto: د امپېر د کړۍ قانون، چې اندري ماري پېټر امپېر په 1826 کې ورکړ، د جریان‌لرونکي سیم شاوخوا په کړۍ کې مدغم مقناطیسي ساحه له هغه جریان سره تړي چې له سیم څخه تېرېږي. د امپېر د کړۍ قانون وايي چې په هره تړلې کړۍ کې د هر اوږدوالي عنصر او له هغه عنصر سره موازي د مقناطیسي ساحې د جز د ضربونو مجموعه د لارې دننه محصور جریان سره متناسب ده. Σ B⃗ · Δl⃗ = μ₀ I

definitions.definition: The permeability of a vacuum (μ₀) is 4π × 10⁻⁷ Wb/(A·m) (webers/ampere-turn·meter) and is used as a reference. The relative permeability (μᵣ) of a material is the ratio of its absolute permeability to the permeability of a vacuum. μᵣ = μ/μ₀ Because it is a ratio of permeabilities, μᵣ is dimensionless. Typical magnetic materials, such as iron, have a relative permeability of a few hundred.

definitions.definition: A coil wound in the form of a spiral (helix) forms a solenoid. When current is passed through a solenoid, a reasonably uniform magnetic field can be produced. This field is strong along the axis of the solenoid and weaker outside, as shown in Figure 13.12.

definitions.definition: RIGHT-HAND RULE III FOR A SOLENOID: Curl the fingers in the direction of current around the coil or solenoid and the extended thumb will point in the direction of the north pole of a magnet. workedExamples.title: Example 13.5 — torque on a square loop
workedExamples.question: A square loop of wire of side 4.0 cm carries 3.0 A of current. A uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.67 T makes an angle of 30° with the plane of the loop. (a) What is the magnitude of the torque on the loop? (b) What is the net magnetic force on the loop?
workedExamples.solution: GIVEN — For a single square loop, number of turns N = 1; magnetic field B = 0.6 T; area A = ab = 4.0 cm × 4.0 cm = 0.0016 m; current I = 3.0 A; angle with plane of loop φ = 30°. REQUIRED — Torque τ = ?; magnetic force F_net = ? SOLUTION — The angle θ between the area vector A and magnetic field B is θ = 90° − φ = 90° − 30° = 60°. (a) The torque on the current-carrying coil is τ = NIAB sin θ. Putting values: τ = 1 × (3.00 A) × 0.0016 m × 0.6 T sin 60°. Hence τ = 2.5 × 10⁻³ Nm. Answer. (b) B sin θ is the same at opposite sides of the loop and opposite sides have equal and opposite forces. The net force is zero: F⃗_net = F⃗_top + F⃗_bottom + F⃗_right + F⃗_left = F⃗_top − F⃗_top + F⃗_right − F⃗_right. Hence F⃗_net = 0 N. Answer.

workedExamples.title: Example 13.6 — converting a galvanometer
workedExamples.question: A galvanometer has a resistance of 100 ohms and gives full-scale deflection on 1 mA current. How can it be converted into (a) an ammeter of range 10 A, and (b) a voltmeter of range 10 V?
workedExamples.solution: GIVEN — Galvanometer resistance R_g = 100 Ω; current through galvanometer I_g = 1 × 10⁻³ A; current range I = 10 A; voltage range V = 10 V. REQUIRED — Shunt resistance R_s = ?; high resistance R_h = ? (a) To convert the galvanometer into an ammeter of range I = 10 A, connect shunt resistance R_s in parallel. R_s = I_gR_g/(I − I_g). Putting values: R_s = (1 × 10⁻³ A × 100 Ω)/(10 A − 1 × 10⁻³ A). Therefore R_s = 0.0100 Ω. Answer. (b) To convert the galvanometer into a voltmeter of range V = 10 V, connect a high resistance R_h in series. R_h = V/I_g − R_g. Putting values: R_h = 10 V/(1 × 10⁻³ A) − 100 Ω. Therefore R_h = 9,900 Ω. Answer.
